text:
anya: Flagging a gap in the active-active write model: when we allow "escrowed" cross-region writes for latency, we need a clear handshake so we don't create split-brain for tenant state. Brain dump of a possible flow below, want pushback.

anya: Escrow write handshake idea:
```
1) client -> region A (near) with X-Write-Escrow: true, idempotency_token
2) A records provisional write (provisional=true), returns 202 + escrow_id
3) A async -> preferred resident region B: verify residency & KMS region match
   - if B accepts, B writes durable record and acknowledges escrow_id
   - if B rejects (policy/KMS mismatch), A marks provisional failed and returns failure to client (or redirects)
4) Once A sees ack from B, A flips provisional->committed and emits commit_audit(escrow_id, actor=system)
5) If ack not received within timeout, A triggers operator-escrow-alert and exposes Cancel/Force options in operator UI
```

mara: Strong 👍 on explicit provisional state. A couple of questions: what's the client-visible model for durability guarantees? 202 + escrow_id is fine but the client needs a way to poll/subscribe for finality. Also want a TTL for provisional so we can GC stranded escrows.

lee: Additions: 1) require a signed consent token for cross-region writes (token includes tenant_id, consent_flags, signer). No token -> immediate 403. 2) include kms_key_id on the provisional record and validate region ownership before commit.

olivia: Ops implications: the operator UI must show a live list of escrows in FAILING state and include a recommended action (retry, force-commit-with-escrow, rollback). Force-commit should be gated and require 2FA + reason_code. All actions emit `escrow_audit` event.

anya: Good call. I propose states: PROVISIONAL -> COMMIT_PENDING (after send to resident) -> COMMITTED | PROVISIONAL_FAILED -> ROLLED_BACK. We should record last_attempt_ts and attempt_count.

sam: One more edge: concurrent writes to same logical key from two different regions. We need a deterministic tie-breaker. Suggest escrow records include write_timestamp and origin_region; resident B only accepts commit if the incoming write_timestamp >= current_version_timestamp OR origin_region == resident_primary for that tenant. Otherwise B returns conflict and preserves resident's version. That ensures resident wins unless client explicitly asked for overwrite and provided override token.

mara: For conflicts we should surface a conflict-resolution policy: REJECT | MERGE | DEFER_TO_OPERATOR. Default for PII-heavy tenants = REJECT. Less sensitive = MERGE with CRDT-lite merge if possible. CRDTs are heavy though; maybe support application-level merge hooks.

lee: Telemetry: emit `escrow_created`, `escrow_forwarded`, `escrow_committed`, `escrow_failed`, `escrow_admin_action`. Include fields: escrow_id, tenant_id, decision_version, kms_region, reason_code (if admin). These are strings in the event stream.

olivia: Also add `X-Escrow-Id` in responses and `X-Routing-Graph` + `X-Decision-Version`. Operator UI can filter by decision_version to correlate why a particular region was chosen.

anya: About timeouts: propose two thresholds: soft_timeout (30s) -> trigger aggressive retry to resident and notify client they are in degraded finalization mode; hard_timeout (5m) -> mark provisional_failed and create operator task. Sticky routing: if a tenant experiences >3 escrows in 10m, route them to resident-first for 1h to avoid repeated cross-region churn.

sam: Sticky-fallback is good. Also: cost accounting — provisional writes should charge a small upfront credit and final charge upon commit. If it fails and is rolled back, refund portion and emit billing_adjustment event. Ops needs visibility.

mara: KMS/E2EE note: For true compliance, resident must hold CMAK (customer-managed key) that strictly keys to resident region. If escrow used, we must ensure wrapped key movement or escrowed-encryption semantics that do not expose plaintext outside resident. That adds complexity but required for some customers.

lee: Implementation detail: keep provisional objects lightweight: only tombstone + metadata + write_digest (hash of payload) + kms_key_ref. Avoid storing full payload twice. Resident B can request full payload from A only when needed (private channel with mTLS).

olivia: Operator guardrails: admin actions: RETRY, FORCE_COMMIT, ROLLBACK. Each requires different approvals: RETRY = manual click; FORCE_COMMIT = 2FA + reason; ROLLBACK = automated policy or 2FA for critical tenants. All go through an internal ticketing event that gets linked to audit logs.

anya: What about reads during provisional? Clients reading the key should get last committed value; provisional shouldn't be visible unless client asks for `?include_provisional=true` and has appropriate consent. Otherwise provisional is hidden.

sam: Good. That prevents accidental exposure. Also we must ensure TTL/Garbage collection: provisional GC after 48h with operator alert before purge.

mara: Simulation plan idea: run a 24h synthetic workload with 50k tenants, 5% with residency constraints, inject network partition between regions for random 10-30s windows, measure: escrow latency distribution, percent forced operator action, number of conflicts. Use that to tune soft/hard timeouts and sticky window.

lee: I'll prototype a small harness and publish a script. Will instrument counters for `escrow_retry_count` and `escrow_conflict_rate`.

olivia: Ops-bot: please add an alert rule: if `escrow_failed_rate` > 0.5% in 10m for global tenants, page oncall and create a high-priority operator queue.

ops-bot: ack: creating alert draft: escrow_failed_rate > 0.005 (10m) -> page SRE, create incident ticket with tag `escrow`.

anya: Action items: 1) I'll write RFC appendix describing escrow handshake and states. 2) @lee prototype sim harness + telemetry names. 3) @mara document dataset-level policies for provisional visibility and conflict policy defaults. 4) @olivia add header stubs and operator UI requirements. 5) ops-bot to draft alert and add as required telemetry.

sam: Thanks — this feels like a clear path. We should also call out which tenants get allowed for escrow by default (probably none; opt-in with explicit consent). We'll surface an admin flag to enable per-tenant.

mara: Agree. Default = disabled. Opt-in via tenant config: allow_escrow_writes: true + consent_token.

lee: I'll send a small PR with the proto messages for escrow events and a skeleton implementation of the provisional record.

anya: Great. Closing the thread for now; RFC follow-up incoming. :rocket:
